hero_role: the generous warrior born with golden armour
title: कर्ण ने अपना कवच क्यों दान कर दिया?
source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (public-domain epic; this retelling is our own)
summary: Karna was born with golden armour and earrings that made him impossible to defeat. Every morning after his prayers to the Sun he gave whatever anyone asked. Before the great war, the god Indra came disguised as a poor brahmin and asked for the armour and earrings. Karna knew who he was and why he had come, yet he would not break his vow of giving. He gave them away without hesitation. Indra, moved by this, gave him a divine spear in return. The lesson: a promise kept at great cost is true greatness.
caption: Karna jaanta tha ki maangne wala kaun hai, phir bhi usne mana nahin kiya.
lines: कर्ण सोने के कवच और कुंडल के साथ जन्मे थे।
हर सुबह सूर्य पूजा के बाद वे हर माँगने वाले को दान देते थे।
एक दिन इंद्र गरीब ब्राह्मण बनकर उनके पास आए।
उन्होंने कर्ण से उनका कवच और कुंडल माँग लिया।
कर्ण सब जानते थे, फिर भी उन्होंने दान कर दिया।
वचन निभाने वाला ही सच्चा महान होता है।

title: अभिमन्यु चक्रव्यूह में अकेला क्यों गया?
source: Mahabharata, Drona Parva (public-domain epic; this retelling is our own)
summary: On the thirteenth day of the war the enemy formed the Chakravyuha, a spiral battle formation. Only Arjuna knew how to break it, and he was fighting far away. His sixteen-year-old son Abhimanyu had learned how to enter the formation but not how to come out. To protect his family's army he chose to enter anyway. He broke through ring after ring with great courage. The others could not follow him in, and he fought on alone. The lesson: courage means stepping forward even when the way back is unknown.
caption: Solah saal ka yoddha, jise andar jaana aata tha, bahar aana nahin.
lines: युद्ध के तेरहवें दिन शत्रु ने चक्रव्यूह रचा।
उसे तोड़ना केवल अर्जुन जानते थे, और वे बहुत दूर थे।
सोलह साल के अभिमन्यु को केवल भीतर जाना आता था।
फिर भी अपनी सेना के लिए वह आगे बढ़ गया।
एक के बाद एक घेरा तोड़ता हुआ वह अकेला लड़ता रहा।
रास्ता न पता हो, फिर भी आगे बढ़ना ही साहस है।

title: कृष्ण ने सुदामा के चावल क्यों खाए?
source: Bhagavata Purana (public-domain text; this retelling is our own)
summary: Sudama was a poor childhood friend of Krishna. He walked to Krishna's golden city of Dwarka carrying only a small bundle of flattened rice as a gift, and felt ashamed of it. Krishna ran to welcome him, washed his feet, and seated him on his own throne. Krishna found the hidden bundle and ate the rice with joy. Sudama asked for nothing and walked home. When he arrived he found his hut had become a beautiful home. The lesson: true friendship does not measure the gift.
caption: Ek mutthi chawal, aur dosti ki sabse badi kahani.
lines: सुदामा कृष्ण के बचपन के गरीब मित्र थे।
वे एक मुट्ठी चावल लेकर द्वारका पहुँचे।
कृष्ण दौड़कर आए और उन्हें गले लगा लिया।
उन्होंने सुदामा के चावल बड़े प्रेम से खाए।
सुदामा बिना कुछ माँगे घर लौट गए।
घर पहुँचे तो झोपड़ी सुंदर महल बन चुकी थी।
सच्ची मित्रता उपहार नहीं तौलती।

hero_role: the strongest of the five brothers
title: भीम एक बूढ़े वानर की पूँछ क्यों नहीं उठा पाए?
source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (public-domain epic; this retelling is our own)
summary: Bhima, proud of his great strength, was walking through a forest to find a divine flower. An old monkey lay across the path with its tail in the way. Bhima ordered it to move. The monkey said it was too old and asked Bhima to lift the tail aside. Bhima tried with one hand, then with all his strength, and could not move it at all. Humbled, he bowed and asked who the monkey was. It was his elder brother Hanuman, who blessed him. The lesson: strength without humility is incomplete.
caption: Sabse balwaan yoddha, aur ek poonch jo hili tak nahin.
lines: भीम को अपने बल पर बहुत गर्व था।
जंगल के रास्ते में एक बूढ़ा वानर लेटा था।
भीम ने कहा, अपनी पूँछ रास्ते से हटाओ।
वानर बोला, मैं बूढ़ा हूँ, तुम ही हटा दो।
भीम ने पूरा ज़ोर लगाया, पर पूँछ हिली तक नहीं।
वह वानर स्वयं हनुमान थे, भीम ने सिर झुका लिया।
विनम्रता के बिना बल अधूरा है।
